How full the model's context is, against the point where efrd compacts it.

A client shows `ctx N%`, where N is `tokens` as a percent of `limit`: 100% means that
a compaction runs now.

limit.description:
The tokens at which a client shows 100%: the auto compaction trigger
(`compaction.auto_at` percent of `window`), or the hard cap (95% of `window`) when
`compaction.auto` is off.

tokens.description:
The tokens in the context: after a model call, its input plus its output; before
a call, efrd's estimate of the request.

window.description:
The context window of the turn's model, in tokens. For a model whose window efr
does not know, the default that efrd counts with.

ConversationCompact.description:
The params of `conversation.compact` (`efr compact [focus]`, `,compact [focus]`).

efrd compacts the context of an idle conversation: it prunes old tool output and,
when that does not free enough room, writes a summary of the history before the
verbatim tail. It records `conversation_compacted` and answers when the compaction
is done. It never starts a turn.

Refusals, each with nothing recorded:

- `conflict` while a turn of the conversation runs: the turn compacts on its own
  when it needs to, so efrd does not wait for it;
- `conflict` when nothing lies before the verbatim tail, so a compaction would free
  no room;
- `not_found` for a conversation that does not exist.

A prompt that arrives while the compaction runs waits in the queue and starts after
it.

command_id.description: Makes the request idempotent: a retry with the same id returns the first result.

focus.description:
What the summary must keep, in the user's words, such as `the failing test and
its fix`. Absent: the summary keeps what its fixed sections ask for.

compaction.description: The compaction, as the event records it.

seq.description: The sequence number of the `conversation_compacted` event.

ConversationContext.description:
The params of `conversation.context`, a read method.

efrd builds the history that the next request of the conversation would send, with
the system prompt and the tool definitions, and measures each part. It never sends
the text of a message: only sizes, counts and the labels that `efr history` shows
already (the command line of a shell call, the path of a file tool, the id of a
job). While a turn runs, the answer holds the turn's messages up to now, from the
log.

Refusals: `not_found` for a conversation that does not exist.

model.description:
The model to measure for. Absent: the model of the newest turn, else the
default model. The model decides the window and whether the provider's own
items of earlier turns go back.

ConversationContextResult.description:
The result of `conversation.context`.

Every token count in `parts`, `largest` and `estimate` is an estimate: the bytes of
the request's JSON divided by 4. The provider's own count (`counted`) differs, mostly
for reasoning and images, and a client shows it first.

cache.description: The cache use of the conversation's model calls.

counted.description:
The provider's last real count: the context at the end of the newest turn.
Absent when no turn has one since the newest compaction.

estimate.description:
The estimated tokens of the next request now, without the next prompt and its
preamble: the sum of `parts`.

hard_cap.description: The largest request that efrd sends: 95% of the window.

largest.description:
The largest single items of the history, largest first: at most
[`MAX_LARGEST`] of them.

model.description: The model that the numbers are for.

parts.description:
What the next request holds, one entry per kind, in the order of
[`ContextPartKind::ALL`]. A kind with nothing in it is absent.

running.description: True when a turn runs: the history holds its messages up to now.

trigger.description: The context size at which an auto compaction runs.

window.description:
The model's context window, in tokens. When efrd does not know it, the default
that efrd counts with.

window_known.description: True when the model list knows the window; false when `window` is the default.

ConversationDelete.description:
The params of `conversation.delete`, a terminal method.

efrd stops the conversation's background jobs and waits for their end, closes its
hidden shell, then records `conversation_deleted` with the receipt. From that event
on, no list, search or read shows the conversation, and the store refuses every new
event of it. Then efrd removes its events, its search index rows, its saved
messages, its receipts, its recordings, its `$SCRATCH`, its sandbox dirs, its
snapshot refs and its undo trash. A stop of efrd in the middle leaves no part of the
conversation visible, and the next start of efrd finishes the removal.

Refusals: `busy` while a turn runs, a prompt waits in its queue, a compaction or an
undo runs, unless `stop` is set; `not_found` for a conversation that does not exist
or that is deleted already.

force.description:
Delete the conversation also when another open terminal holds it. Without it,
efrd deletes nothing and answers `held`.

stop.description:
Stop the running turn, the queued prompts, a compaction or an undo first.
Without it, efrd deletes nothing and answers `busy` while one of them runs.

oneOf.description: The conversation is deleted.

jobs_stopped.description: The background jobs that efrd stopped first. Absent when none.

not_removed.description:
The files and dirs of the conversation that efrd could not remove. The next
start of efrd tries again. Absent when none.

title.description: Its title, for the line of the client.

oneOf.description:
Another open terminal holds the conversation, and `force` was not set: nothing
changed.

title.description: The conversation's title, for the question.

oneOf.description: An answer from a newer daemon.

ConversationDiff.description:
The params of `conversation.diff`, a read method.

The daemon compares the turn's first snapshot (before its first call that can
write) with its last (at turn end), in each registered project and `$SCRATCH` that
the turn wrote through its calls.

conversation_id.description:
The conversation. Absent: the conversation of `turn_id`, else the active
conversation of the terminal that the connection's `hello` named.

stat.description: True asks for the list of files only, without the unified diff.

turn_id.description:
The turn. Absent: the newest finished turn of the conversation. A turn that ran
no call that can write has no snapshots, and its list of files is empty.

diff.description:
The unified diff of every changed file, with the paths of
[`FileChange::path`](crate::FileChange::path) after `a/` and `b/`, at most
[`MAX_TURN_DIFF_LINES`](crate::MAX_TURN_DIFF_LINES) lines and then a line
`... N more lines`. Absent with `stat`.

turn_id.description: The turn that the answer is about.

cursor.description:
Where to continue: a `next_cursor` or a snapshot's `history_cursor`. Absent for
the most recent page.

limit.description: The most events to return; the daemon picks a default and a maximum.

events.description: One page of events, oldest first.

next_cursor.description:
The cursor for the page of older events; absent when this page reaches the first
event.

ConversationId.description: One conversation: the unit a `,` line talks to and a subscription follows.

ConversationResume.description:
The params of `conversation.resume`, an operate method.

The conversation goes into the slot of its own scope key in the terminal of
`context`, and that slot becomes the terminal's current one: efrd records
`terminal_attached` (`how: resumed`). Another terminal that held it lets it go, and
its next prompt there says where it went. When the conversation has no hidden shell
that runs, efrd starts one in its last directory.

Refusals: `invalid` for a context without a tty, `forbidden` for a connection that
is not the shell's or `efr`'s on that terminal (a phone, a made-up tty), and
`not_found` for a conversation that does not exist.

context.description:
The terminal's shell, as the zsh plugin observed it: its `tty` and `shell_pid`
name the terminal and the shell that hold the conversation, and its `pwd` says
whether the next prompt continues it.

take.description:
Move the conversation also when another open terminal holds it. Without it,
efrd moves nothing and answers `held`.

oneOf.description: The conversation is the terminal's conversation for its scope now.

continues_here.description:
True when a prompt from the working directory of the params continues it:
the directory is in its scope, or `conversation.follow_project` is off.

here.description:
True when the terminal held it already: the resume only made its slot the
current one.

scope.description: Its scope: the slot of the terminal that holds it now.

shell_dir.description:
The directory of its hidden shell: where efrd started it, or where the
shell that runs is. Absent when no shell could start.

updated_at.description: When it was last active, before the resume.

oneOf.description:
Another open terminal holds the conversation, and `take` was not set: nothing
moved.

title.description: The conversation's title, for the question.

oneOf.description: An answer from a newer daemon.

ConversationSearch.description:
The params of `conversation.search`, a read method for user-side peers: the hits in
one conversation.

efrd reads `query` as `conversations.search` does. `not_found` for a conversation
that does not exist.

limit.description: The most hits to return: 20 when absent, 50 at most.

query.description:
The words to find. Empty after a trim: the newest prompts and the start of the
newest answer, with no ranges.

hits.description:
The hits, newest first: at most 12 lines each, and a line of at most 400
characters, which ends with `...` when efrd cut it.

partial.description: Why the search stopped before it saw every match. Absent: it saw every match.

title.description:
The title with its secrets replaced, and the parts that match. Absent before
efrd indexed the conversation, and for a conversation without a title.

ConversationSnapshot.description: A bounded view of a conversation: its summary and its most recent events.

conversation.description: The conversation as a list shows it.

events.description: The most recent events, oldest first.

history_cursor.description:
The cursor for `conversation.history` to page through the events before
`events`; absent when `events` starts at the beginning.

hwm.description:
The sequence number that the snapshot is complete up to. Live events after it
follow.

live.description:
What the running turn has so far, when a turn runs: the text of its current
message and its reasoning, which `events` can miss. Only a daemon that announces
`snapshot_live` sends it.

oneOf.description: No turn is running.
A turn is running.
A turn waits for the user to answer an approval request.

ConversationSubscribe.description:
The params of `conversation.subscribe`, a streaming method.

With `after_seq`, the daemon replays the events after it when the gap is small (at
most 128 events or 1 MiB) and otherwise sends a bounded snapshot; without it, the
stream starts with a snapshot. Live events follow, each with a larger sequence number
than anything sent before. A subscriber that falls behind its bounded queue is closed
with `overflow` and its `last_seq`, and subscribes again from there.

after_seq.description: The largest sequence number the client has already seen.

answers_input.description:
True when a person at this client can type answers to a running command that
waits for input, with `input.respond`. The daemon stops a command that waits for
hidden input, such as a password, when no live subscription of its conversation
can answer. Absent means false, so an older client counts as one that cannot.

drafts.description:
True when the client wants [`Draft`] items: the text, the reasoning and the
tool input of a running turn as they arrive from the model, before the event
log has them. Absent means false, so an older client gets no drafts.

oneOf.description: One event, replayed or live.

A bounded view of the conversation, sent instead of a replay that would be too
large.

What a running turn got from the model since the last draft. Only a subscriber
that asked for `drafts` gets it. It is not an event: it has no sequence number
of its own, and the daemon does not store it.

ConversationSummary.description: What a list shows about one conversation.

cwd.description: The user's working directory at the last prompt.

last_seq.description: The sequence number of its last event.

scope.description: The scope of the last turn.

status.description: What the conversation is doing now.

title.description: A short title, taken from the first prompt until something better exists.

tty.description:
The terminal that holds the conversation, when one does: it is that terminal's
conversation for its scope.

updated_at.description: When its last event was recorded.

cursor.description:
Where to continue: the `next_cursor` of the previous page. Absent for the first
page.

limit.description: The most conversations to return; the daemon picks a default and a maximum.

tty.description:
Only the conversations of this terminal, its current one first: the one of its
last prompt, `,new` or resume. One page holds them all, with no cursor. A daemon
from before routing by scope ignores it and lists every conversation.

conversations.description: One page of conversations, the most recently updated first.

next_cursor.description: The cursor for the next page; absent on the last page.

ConversationsRecent.description:
The params of `conversations.recent`, a read method.

efrd lists the conversations whose scope key is the key of `pwd` first, newest
first by their last activity, then all others, newest first. Only efrd knows the
key of a directory and which terminal holds a conversation, so the order is
efrd's.

limit.description: The most conversations to return; efrd picks a default of 10 and a maximum.

pwd.description:
The working directory that decides which scope comes first. Absent: newest
first only.

tty.description:
The terminal that asks, such as `/dev/pts/3`: its conversations show as `here`,
and `current` names its current one. Absent for a client without a terminal,
such as the phone.

conversations.description: The conversations, the ones of the scope of `pwd` first, each part newest first.

current.description:
The current conversation of the terminal: the one of its last prompt, `,new`
or resume. Absent without a `tty`, or when the terminal holds none.

scope.description: The scope of `pwd`, whose conversations come first. Absent without a `pwd`.

ConversationsSearch.description:
The params of `conversations.search`, a read method for user-side peers: one row per
conversation.

efrd searches an index of the titles, the user's prompts, the model's answers and
the commands that the agent ran. The index holds no command output and no file
contents, and its text has the secrets that efr recognises replaced. efrd parses
`query` itself, so a client never sends search syntax: words split on white space,
a `"double quoted"` part is one phrase, every word must match in one prompt, answer
or command, and only the last word matches as a prefix. A query of more than 256
characters or 16 words is `invalid`.

limit.description: The most rows to return: 50 when absent, 200 at most.

pwd.description:
The working directory that decides the current scope, for an empty query.
Absent: no scope comes first.

query.description:
The words to find. Empty after a trim: the recent conversations, in the order of
`conversations.recent`.

stats.description: Also return the measures of the search in `stats`. False when absent.

tty.description:
The terminal that asks, such as `/dev/pts/3`: its conversations show as `here`,
and `current` names its current one. Absent on the phone.

current.description:
The current conversation of the terminal, as in `conversations.recent`. Absent
without a `tty`, or when the terminal holds none.

index.description: How far efrd has indexed the conversations. Absent: the index is complete.

partial.description: Why the search stopped before it saw every match. Absent: it saw every match.

rows.description:
The rows, best first. For an empty query: the ones of the scope of `pwd` first,
each part newest first.

scope.description:
The scope of `pwd`, whose conversations come first, for an empty query only:
the same as in `conversations.recent`. Absent for a query and without a `pwd`.

stats.description: The measures of the search, when the params asked for them.

ConversationsWatch.description:
The params of `conversations.watch`, a streaming read method.

The stream starts with a `snapshot`: the recent conversations of the machine, newest
first by their last activity, as `conversations.recent` without a `tty` and a `pwd`
gives them. Then efrd sends `changed` each time a commit changes what a list shows
of a conversation: its title, its status, its working directory, its scope, its
project or its count of turns. A commit that changes only the time and the sequence
number of the last activity sends nothing. A conversation that is not in the
snapshot gets `changed` at its first such commit. `removed` follows the delete of a
conversation.

A subscriber that falls behind is closed with `overflow`. It then watches again and
gets a new snapshot. The `last_seq` of that error names the last commit that the
stream looked at, and a new watch does not use it.

limit.description:
The most conversations of the snapshot; efrd picks a default of 20 and a
maximum of 50.

oneOf.description: The recent conversations, newest first. Always the first item.

conversations.description:
The rows, as `conversations.recent` gives them. `here` is false and
`open_in` names a terminal that held the conversation when efrd read it.

oneOf.description:
What a list shows of one conversation changed, or the stream did not show it
before. The row replaces the row with the same id.

conversation.description: The row now. Boxed, so the other items stay small.

oneOf.description: The conversation was deleted. A list drops its row.

CountedUse.description: The provider's own count of the context at the end of a turn.

tokens.description:
The tokens in the context at the last model call of the turn: its input plus its
output.

Cursor.description: The cursor position in the visible grid, counted from 0 at the top left.

col.description: The column, from 0 at the left edge.

hidden.description: True when the program has hidden the cursor.

row.description: The row, from 0 at the top of the visible grid.

DaemonId.description:
The identity of one daemon installation, created at its first start. Clients pin
it, so they notice when a socket path leads to a different daemon.

DaemonPaths.description: Directories of the daemon that clients show to the user.

data_dir.description: The daemon's data directory: the database, recordings and secrets.

scratch_root.description: The parent of every conversation's `$SCRATCH` directory.

config.description: The config root, which holds `config.toml` and `projects.toml`.

data.description: The data root: the database, recordings, scratch directories and secrets.

runtime.description: The runtime root: the socket and `daemon.json`.

DesktopEnv.description:
The desktop variables of the user's shell, as the shell has them. Only these six
names, never another variable, and whether the shell has `$XAUTHORITY`. efrd checks
each value before it binds a socket.

has_xauthority.description:
True when the shell has `$XAUTHORITY`, so its X server needs a cookie. Only
that the variable is set, never its path: the cookie file stays masked.

wayland_display.description: `$WAYLAND_DISPLAY`: a socket name below `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, or an absolute path.

DesktopKind.description:
A desktop whose control socket a [`Grant::Desktop`] binds: the compositor or the
window manager that a program such as `hyprctl` or `swaymsg` talks to.

oneOf.description: A Wayland compositor, through `$WAYLAND_DISPLAY`.
An X server on this machine, through a local `$DISPLAY`.
Hyprland's control socket, `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypr/<signature>/.socket.sock`.
Sway's IPC socket, `$SWAYSOCK`.
i3's IPC socket, `$I3SOCK`.
niri's socket, `$NIRI_SOCKET`.

DeviceEnroll.description:
The params of `device.enroll`, a remote method that runs before the proof.

The daemon checks the token, shows the phone's facts at the terminal and answers
only after the terminal confirms. A wrong or used token is `unauthorized`; a no at
the terminal, or a pairing that expires, is `forbidden`. The phone checks
`daemon_id` and `protocol` of the `hello` result against the QR code before it
sends the token. The Unix socket refuses the method.

name.description:
The name of the device, such as `Anna's iPhone`, for the terminal and for
`device.list`.

public_key.description:
The device's P-256 public key: the 65-byte uncompressed point (`04`, then X and
Y), as standard base64.

token.description: The token of the QR code.

device_id.description:
The new device. The phone keeps it and proves its key with `device.prove` on
this connection and on each one after it.

scopes.description: What the device may do once it proved its key.

DeviceId.description: An enrolled device such as a phone. The Unix socket does not use it.

DeviceInfo.description: One enrolled device, as `device.list` shows it.

created_at.description: When the terminal confirmed the device.

key_fingerprint.description:
A short fingerprint of the device's public key, to compare with what the phone
shows.

last_seen_at.description:
When the device last proved its key; absent when it never connected after it
enrolled.

name.description: The name that the device sent when it enrolled, such as `Anna's iPhone`.

node.description:
The stable id of the Tailscale node that the device enrolled from. A connection
from another node does not prove this device.

revoked_at.description: When the device was revoked; absent while it may connect.

DeviceList.description: The params of `device.list`, an admin method (Unix socket only). It takes none.

devices.description: Every enrolled device, the revoked ones too, the oldest first.

DevicePairConfirm.description:
The params of `device.pair_confirm`, an admin method (Unix socket only). It answers
the `pending` item of a `device.pair_start` stream.

A pairing that is not pending, or that ended, is `not_found`.

accept.description: True to enroll the device, false to refuse it.

device_id.description: The new device; absent when the answer was no.

DevicePairStart.description:
The params of `device.pair_start`, a streaming admin method (Unix socket only).

The daemon makes a one-time token and sends the `started` item with the QR code.
When a phone sends that token with `device.enroll`, the daemon sends `pending`
with the facts of the phone, and the terminal answers with `device.pair_confirm`.
The stream then sends `paired` or `ended` and ends. A cancel of the request, or the
end of the connection, ends the pairing: the token is then good for nothing.

name.description: The name to give the device. Absent: the name that the phone sends.

oneOf.description: The pairing is open: show the QR code. Always the first item.

qr.description: What the QR code holds; [`PairingQr::url`] is its text.

oneOf.description:
A phone sent the token. The daemon waits for `device.pair_confirm`. The user
compares these facts with the phone before saying yes.

device_name.description: The name that the phone sent.

key_fingerprint.description: The fingerprint of the phone's key, which the phone shows too.

node_name.description: The name of the phone's Tailscale node.

os.description:
The operating system of the phone's node, such as `iOS`, when Tailscale
knows it.

user_login.description:
The login of the Tailscale user of the phone's node, such as
`anna@example.com`. For display only.

oneOf.description: The terminal said yes and the device is enrolled. The last item.
The pairing ended without a device. The last item.

DeviceProve.description:
The params of `device.prove`, a remote method that runs before the proof.

The device signs [`ProveMessage::to_bytes`](crate::ProveMessage::to_bytes) of the
`hello` result's `challenge`, `daemon_id`, `protocol` and `prove` facts. Before this
method succeeds, a remote connection may call only `hello`, `device.enroll` and
`device.prove`. A wrong signature, or a device that is revoked or that enrolled from
another node, is `unauthorized`; the daemon closes the connection after a few
failed proofs. The Unix socket refuses the method.

device_id.description: The device. When the `hello` sent a `device_id`, it is the same.

signature.description:
The ECDSA P-256 signature with SHA-256 of the message, in DER, as standard
base64.

scopes.description: What the connection may do now.

DeviceRevoke.description:
The params of `device.revoke`, an admin method (Unix socket only).

The daemon marks the device revoked and closes its open connections at once. A
device that does not exist is `not_found`. A revoke of a revoked device changes
nothing.

revoked_at.description: When the device was revoked: now, or the time of the first revoke.

Draft.description:
A draft: part of a running turn as it arrives from the model, before the event log
has it.

Drafts are best effort. The daemon sends at most one draft of each part per
`conversation.draft_interval_ms` (the first one at once). When the subscriber's
queue is full, it merges the drafts of each part that wait and sends them at the
next free place (the capability `drafts_coalesced`), so a slow subscriber gets
fewer, larger drafts with no gap. It never closes a subscription because of a draft.
The events stay the source of truth: `assistant_message_updated` and
`assistant_message_completed` carry the same text at the same offsets.

after_seq.description:
The sequence number of the last event that the turn recorded before it made
this draft. Every event of the stream at or below it comes before the draft. An
event of the turn with a larger number came after the draft. The daemon does
not send a draft that is older than an `assistant_message_completed`, a
`tool_call_started` or the end of a turn that it sent on the stream before.

turn_id.description: The turn that the draft belongs to.

DraftPart.description: The part of a running turn that a [`Draft`] carries.

oneOf.description:
More text of an assistant message. `index`, `offset` and `delta` have the
meaning that they have in `assistant_message_updated`: `offset` is the byte
offset of `delta` in the whole text of message `index`. Drafts and updates count
the same text, so a client can merge the two.

index.description:
The position of the message among the assistant messages of the turn that
have text, from 0. A model answer without text takes no position.

offset.description:
The offset of `delta` in the text of the message, in bytes of UTF-8. It is
not a count of characters or of UTF-16 units: a JavaScript client compares
it with the UTF-8 length of its text, never with `text.length`.

oneOf.description:
More of the reasoning summary of the model. Reasoning never goes into the event
log.

offset.description:
The offset of `delta` in the reasoning text of the whole turn, in bytes of
UTF-8. The reasoning of a later model call in the same turn continues the
text after a blank line.

title.description:
The title of the newest reasoning section: the last line of the reasoning
so far that is all bold (`**Title**`), without the stars. Absent until
such a line comes.

oneOf.description:
The model writes the input of a tool call. `tool_call_started` comes only
after the whole answer of the model is in.

bytes.description:
How many bytes of input the model has written so far: of the JSON
arguments, or of the text of a freeform tool such as `apply_patch`.

call.description:
The position of the call among the tool calls of this answer of the model,
from 0, so a client can tell two calls of one answer apart.

oneOf.description:
How full the model's context is. The turn sends it before each model call, with
its estimate of the request, and after each call, with the count that the
provider reported. A client shows it as `ctx N%` while the turn runs.

The turn compacts the context before its next model call. A client shows
`compacting context` until the `conversation_compacted` event, the next
`context` draft or the end of the turn, whichever comes first.

EffectiveSettings.description:
The settings that a turn runs with: the prompt's [`TurnSettings`] over the config's
defaults, checked by the daemon.

effort.description:
The reasoning effort; absent when none is sent, so the backend uses its own
default for the model.

fallback.description:
Why the turn runs with a stricter mode than it asked for, such as `auto` without
a working sandbox; `mode` is the mode it runs with. Absent when it runs with the
mode it asked for.

mode.description:
The permission mode. For a turn from a remote origin it is at most `cautious`,
whatever the prompt or the config asked for.

overridden.description:
Which values came from the prompt rather than from the config. Absent when none
did.

provider.description:
The provider that runs the turn, such as `anthropic-api`. Absent from a daemon
before it recorded the provider.

ErrorBody.description:
The body of an error: a code to act on, a message for a person, and optional data
whose shape depends on the code.

data.description:
Structured details. [`ErrorCode::Overflow`] carries `{"last_seq": n}` and
[`ErrorCode::ProtocolMismatch`] carries `{"daemon": n, "client": m}`.

message.description: One sentence for a person. Clients show it; they never parse it.

ErrorCode.description:
What went wrong with a request, as a closed set that every client can handle.

The set is closed on the wire: a new code is a breaking change and bumps
[`PROTOCOL_VERSION`](crate::PROTOCOL_VERSION). The mapping from the daemon's own
errors to these codes lives in one place, `efr-daemon/src/error.rs`.

oneOf.description:
The client and the daemon speak different protocol versions. Sent in answer to
`hello`, before any other method runs.
The connection has not proven who it is.
The connection is known but lacks the scope that the method needs.
A conversation, turn, approval or PTY that the request names does not exist.
The request contradicts the current state, such as steering a finished turn.
The daemon cannot take the request now; the client may retry later.

A subscriber fell behind its bounded queue and was closed. The error data holds
`last_seq`, the last sequence number it received, to resume from.
The request was cancelled by its client or by the daemon shutting down.
The frame or its parameters are malformed.
The daemon failed in a way that is not the client's fault.

ErrorFrame.description:
A server frame that ends a request with an error: `{id, error}`.

`id` is absent only when the server could not read a request id from the frame it
rejects; the server then closes the connection.

anyOf.description: A conversation began.

route.description:
The scope key of its first prompt: with `tty`, the terminal's slot that it
takes. Absent in conversations from before routing by scope, and when the
first prompt had no working directory.

tty.description: The terminal it is the active conversation of, when it came from a shell.

anyOf.description:
The conversation became the conversation of a terminal for one scope key,
because a prompt from a new terminal picked it up or the user resumed it there.
The terminal's slot for that key held another conversation before, or none; the
slot of another terminal that held this conversation lets it go.

route.description: The scope key of the slot.

shell_pid.description: The pid of the shell that took it, when it said.

anyOf.description:
A prompt was accepted and waits for its turn. Prompts sent while a turn runs queue
behind it.

command_id.description: The client's id for the `prompt.send` that carried it.

context.description:
The user's shell when the prompt was sent. A [`ShellContext`] holds no command
line, so this event, which the log keeps forever and every subscriber receives,
never carries the last command of `prompt.send`.

settings.description:
The settings that the prompt asked for, kept with it while it waits, so a held
prompt runs with them too. Absent means none.

steers.description:
The `turn_steered` events whose text this prompt carries, when an interrupt
sent unread steers again as a prompt (`turn.interrupt` with
`resend_steers`). A client shows those steers as this prompt from now on.
Absent means none.

turn_id.description: The turn that will answer the prompt.

anyOf.description:
A waiting prompt was taken out of the queue (`prompt.withdraw`, or
`turn.interrupt` with `withdraw`). Its turn never starts, and this is the turn's
last event.

turn_id.description: The turn of the withdrawn prompt.

anyOf.description:
A queued prompt was held after a daemon restart. Only logs from earlier daemons
hold it: a daemon now records a waiting prompt as not run with
[`Event::TurnCancelled`] at the next start, and the one after that settles a held
prompt the same way.

turn_id.description: The turn of the held prompt.

anyOf.description: A turn began running.

cwd.description: The user's working directory when the prompt was sent.

scope.description: The scope derived from that directory.

settings.description:
The settings that the turn runs with until it ends. Absent in turns recorded
before turn settings, whose model and effort no event names.

anyOf.description: The scope of the conversation changed between turns, because the user moved.

turn_id.description: The turn whose working directory produced the new scope.

anyOf.description:
An assistant message grew while the model streamed it. The event carries only
the text added since the previous update, so a long answer costs the log its
length once rather than once per update; `assistant_message_completed` carries
the whole text. A reader that joined in the middle of a message (`offset` past
what it holds) waits for the completed text.

index.description:
The position of the message among the turn's assistant messages that have
text, from 0. A model answer without text takes no position.

offset.description:
The length of the message's text before `delta`, in bytes of UTF-8: not a
count of characters or of UTF-16 units.

anyOf.description: An assistant message is complete.

index.description:
The position of the message among the turn's assistant messages that have
text, from 0. A model answer without text takes no position.

anyOf.description: The model asked for a tool call.

freeform.description:
True when the model wrote the input as plain text for a freeform tool, such
as the patch of an `apply_patch` call for an OpenAI model: `input` is then a
JSON string with that text, and the next request sends the call back in its
freeform form. False when absent: `input` is the JSON that the model wrote,
or a JSON string with arguments that were not JSON.

input.description:
The tool's input as the model wrote it. For a call with `freeform`, a JSON
string that holds the text.

launch.description:
How a `shell` call runs: typed into the hidden shell, in the `auto` sandbox
with its grants, or in the exit child. Absent for other tools and in calls
recorded before the sandbox.

manual_input.description:
True when the call takes an input that the user chooses to type while it
reports no wait (`input.respond` with `manual`), as a `shell` call does whose
command does not type into a shell that reads command lines. A client offers
such an input only for a call with this flag. False when absent.

tool.description: The tool's registered name, such as `shell` or `read_file`.

anyOf.description: A running tool call produced more output. The daemon coalesces updates per call.

bytes.description: The size of the whole output so far, in bytes.

tail.description: The end of the output so far, bounded in size.

anyOf.description:
A running tool call began or stopped waiting for the user to type a line. The
daemon reports each change once. A client that can read keys asks the user while
the call's latest `input` is not `none`, and sends the answer with
`input.respond`; the call's `tool_call_completed` ends the wait as well.

input.description: What the call waits for now.

looks_secret.description:
True for a `visible` wait whose prompt line looks like a password prompt
(`password`, `passphrase`, `passcode`, `PIN`, `verification code` or
`one-time code`) while the terminal is not in line mode, as behind a relay such
as `sudo`'s own pty, `ssh` or `docker exec`. The program on the inner terminal
decides whether the answer is shown, so a client hides what the user types
and says so; the answer is still sent as a visible one. False when absent.

anyOf.description: A tool call finished.

changes.description:
The files that the call changed: for a file tool, the files it wrote, deleted
or moved; for a `shell` call, what changed in the turn's registered project, `$SCRATCH` and,
in `auto`, the registered projects that the line names, as efr's own
snapshots before and after the call show it. Absent when nothing changed
there, for a tool that cannot write, and when efr took no snapshot.

diff.description:
The unified diff of a file tool's call: the diff of each file it changed, in
the order it changed them, one after the other, each with its two header
lines (`/dev/null` for a new or a deleted file), together at most
[`MAX_CALL_DIFF_LINES`](crate::MAX_CALL_DIFF_LINES) lines and then a line
`... N more lines`. Absent for other tools, for a binary file and when no
content changed.

exit_code.description: The exit code, for a tool that runs a command.

is_error.description: True when the tool failed or the call was denied.

left_running.description:
True when a `shell` call answered the model while its command still runs in
the conversation's hidden shell, such as after its timeout. The shell takes
no other call until that command ends; `shell_command_detached` and
`shell_command_ended` of the same `call_id` tell more. A client shows that
the command still runs, not that it ended. False when absent.

output.description: The output that the model sees, truncated in the middle when it is long.

refusal.description:
Why efr refused the call before it ran, in a few words for a person, such as
`efr's config (floor)`. Absent for a call that ran, and for one that the user
denied or that no answer reached.

sandbox.description:
What a call through the sandbox's launcher did to the state around it: names
only, never values. Absent for a call that did not use the launcher.

truncated.description: True when `output` was truncated; the full output stays in the recording.

anyOf.description: A tool call needs the user's approval before it runs.

diff_preview.description: A diff of the change, for a call that writes a file.

exit.description:
What the call would do outside the `auto` sandbox, for an exit. A client that
does not know it shows `summary` as before.

expires_in_secs.description:
How many seconds the question waits before the call does not run, for a
question with a fixed limit, such as a delete that full mode guards. Absent:
no fixed limit.

interactive.description:
True when the call may wait for input at the terminal, such as a `sudo`
password: a client whose user approves it may keep the keys typed while it
runs for the answer it asks for. False when absent.

local_only.description:
True when only the user's own machine may answer, as for a privilege exit,
a delete that full mode guards or a job's question: the daemon refuses an
answer from a phone, and the question stays open. False when absent, also
from a daemon that does not announce `approval_local_only`.

reason.description:
Why the turn's permission mode asks, in one plain line for a person, such as
`cautious asks before any network access.` A client shows it below the
summary. Absent: no reason, also from a daemon that does not set it.

summary.description: What the call would do, in one line.

turn_id.description: The turn, which waits for the answer.

anyOf.description: The user answered an approval request.

An approval request can no longer be answered: it waited longer than its
timeout, the turn was interrupted, or the daemon restarted while it was pending.
The call did not run.

away.description: True when nobody answered while the user was away (`presence.away_wait_secs`).

anyOf.description: The user added guidance to the running turn.

A model call of the turn read these steers: the daemon records it before or
with the model call that sends them to the model. A client moves each steer
from its unread list into the conversation. A steer that no
`steering_delivered` names was never read by the model.

steers.description: The `turn_steered` events that the call read, in sequence order.

anyOf.description:
The user took back steers of the turn that no model call read
(`turn.interrupt` with `withdraw_steers`, Ctrl+C in the input row of a turn). No
model call reads them, and they do not count as sent: a client shows them as
taken back, as a `prompt_withdrawn` prompt.

origin.description: The surface that took them back.

steers.description: The `turn_steered` events that the user took back, in sequence order.

anyOf.description:
The user asked to interrupt the turn. The turn ends with
[`Event::TurnInterrupted`] once the model's stream actually stops.
An interrupted turn stopped.

changes.description:
The files that the turn changed before it stopped, as for
[`Event::TurnCompleted`]. Absent when nothing changed, and in turns recorded
before efr reported it.

context.description:
How full the model's context was when the turn stopped. Absent in turns
recorded before efr counted it.

undo.description:
What `efr undo` can take back of the turn. Absent when the turn has no
snapshot, and in turns recorded before undo.

usage.description:
The tokens that the turn used before it stopped, when the provider reported
them.

anyOf.description: A turn finished normally.

changes.description:
The files that the turn changed: its first snapshot against its last, in the
turn's registered project, `$SCRATCH` and the registered projects that its
calls wrote. Absent when nothing changed there. `conversation.diff` returns
the diff.

context.description:
How full the model's context was when the turn ended. Absent in turns
recorded before efr counted it.

stop.description:
Why the model stopped, when its last call gave no text and no tool call, or
stopped for another reason than the end of its answer. Absent for a normal
answer, and in turns recorded before efr reported it.

undo.description:
What `efr undo` can take back of the turn. Absent when the turn has no
snapshot, and in turns recorded before undo.

usage.description: The tokens that the turn used, when the provider reported them.

anyOf.description: A turn ended with an error, such as a provider failure.

changes.description:
The files that the turn changed before it failed, as for
[`Event::TurnCompleted`]. Absent when nothing changed, and in turns recorded
before efr reported it.

context.description:
How full the model's context was when the turn failed. Absent in turns
recorded before efr counted it.

undo.description:
What `efr undo` can take back of the turn. Absent when the turn has no
snapshot, and in turns recorded before undo.

usage.description:
The tokens that the turn used before it failed, when the provider reported
them.

anyOf.description:
A turn that was running or waiting when the daemon stopped was cancelled at the
next start. Without a [`Event::TurnStarted`] before it, the turn never ran: its
prompt was queued, and the user is told to send it again. Nothing continues on
its own after a restart.
The conversation's hidden shell started.

cwd.description: The directory the shell started in.

anyOf.description: The conversation's hidden shell exited.

exit_code.description: The exit code; absent when a signal ended the shell.

anyOf.description: The hidden shell reported a new working directory (OSC 7).

host.description: The host in the report, when it named one.

anyOf.description: A provider login finished and its credentials are stored.

`admin.logout` deleted the stored credentials of a provider. It holds no part of
them.

A `shell` call in `auto` leaves the sandbox: the exits, what an approval opens,
and the record that a classifier would judge (phase A), stored once per call.

record.description:
The facts of the exit. Boxed, because it is much larger than every other
event.

anyOf.description:
An exit was judged: by the user, by a floor before any question, by the
classifier (phase A) or by an always-allow rule (phase E).

cached.description: True when the verdict came from the turn's cache.

category.description: The classifier's policy category, or the floor's rule.

chain_step.description: The step of the classifier's chain that gave the verdict.

latency_ms.description: How long the classifier took, in milliseconds.

reasked.description:
True when the classifier model wrote no real reason (empty, too short or a
placeholder) and the judge asked it once more. Absent when false, and from an
earlier daemon.

record_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the record the classifier saw, in hex.

skipped.description: The models that the classifier's chain skipped, each as `<model>: <reason>`.

user_authorization.description: The classifier's view of the user's authorization.

anyOf.description:
What became of the rule of an `allow_always` answer (phase E). The turn records
it after it tried to save the rule. `approval_resolved` came before it, when the
answer came.

call_id.description: The call whose question offered the rule.

outcome.description: The saved rule, or why there is none.

anyOf.description:
The classifier started to review an exit, so a client can show `reviewing:`. A
verdict from the turn's cache has none.

The classifier stopped for the rest of the turn after too many denials: each
later exit asks the user, or stops the turn while the user is away.

denials.description: The denials that the limit counted: in a row, or in the turn.

anyOf.description:
The presence of a conversation changed: a person is there to answer its questions,
or not.

efrd deleted paths in the real tool caches that a call had deleted in its private
layer, after the classifier or the user allowed it. Names only.

call_id.description: The call that deleted them in its layer.

freed_bytes.description: The bytes that the deletes freed.

anyOf.description:
A call changed a file outside the project, such as `~/.zshrc`, for the line at
the end of the turn. Names only. Phase A sent it for a file that runs code later,
with `backup`. From phase B efrd sends it for each changed file outside the
roots, with `covered` and no `backup`.

backup.description:
The copy of the file before the call, in efr's phase A backup store. Absent
from phase B.

covered.description:
True when efr copied the file into its home store before the call, so
`efr undo` can bring it back.

floor.description: True when the file is a floor.

real.description:
The real file, absolute, when `path` reaches it through a link, such as a
dotfile link into `~/dotfiles`. Absent when `path` is the real file, and in
events recorded before efr reported it.

anyOf.description:
The surface guard found git settings or other files that run code, which a call
changed. Names only.

call_id.description: The call that made the changes.

quarantined.description: True when at least one change went to quarantine.

anyOf.description:
The turn asks the user whether to keep quarantined changes before its next
call. It is not an approval of a tool call: the call already ended.

call_id.description: The call that made the changes; it does not wait.

turn_id.description: The turn, which waits for the answer.

anyOf.description:
A quarantine question was answered, expired or ended with an interrupt. Only a
"keep" from the user moves the changes back.

keep.description: True when the changes moved back; false leaves them in quarantine.

origin.description:
The surface that answered; absent when the question expired or the turn was
interrupted.

anyOf.description:
At the end of an `auto` turn: the files it changed that run code later outside
the sandbox.

efrd compacted the conversation's context: it pruned old tool output, wrote a
summary of the history before a cut, or both. The model's next request starts
from the compaction (the README of `efr-conversation`, section "Context"). Every
event stays in the log; `efr history` marks the place.

The sandbox probe's result changed to unavailable: `auto` turns run as
`cautious` until it is available again.

efr took a snapshot of a root for a turn: once per root before the turn's first
call that can write it and once at the turn's end, both sent at the turn's end,
and once per copy of files outside the roots.

commit.description: The snapshot's commit in efr's store, in hex.

ms.description: How long the snapshot took, in milliseconds.

root.description:
The root as a client shows it: the project's name, `$SCRATCH`, or `home` for
a copy of files outside the roots.

skipped.description: The files that the snapshot left out, such as large or ignored files.

anyOf.description:
`turn.undo` took back the changes of a turn, or a redo took back an undo. It
belongs to the conversation, not to a turn: `undone_turn_id` names the turn.

conflicts.description: The paths that the undo skipped, because they changed after the turn.

deleted.description: The links and empty entries that the undo removed.

not_covered.description: The paths that no snapshot covers, so the undo left them as they are.

redo.description: True for a redo. False when absent.

refs.description: The refs that the undo moved, or tried to. Absent when none.

restored.description: The files that the undo wrote back.

stopped.description:
True when the undo stopped at a write that failed, after it changed some
paths; the next `efr undo` finishes it. False when absent.

trash.description: The directory of the undo trash. Absent when the undo put nothing there.

trashed.description: The files that the undo moved to the undo trash.

undone_turn_id.description: The turn whose changes the undo took back.

anyOf.description:
A `shell` call with `background: true` started a job, which runs on after the
call answered and after its turn ended. efrd records it before the call answers.

launcher_pid.description: The process id of the job's launcher, which efrd started.

launcher_start.description:
The start time of the launcher's process, in clock ticks after boot (the
22nd field of `/proc/<pid>/stat`), so that a later efrd signals the launcher
and never another process that got its pid.

anyOf.description:
A line of a job's output matched the job's `watch` pattern. It belongs to the
conversation, not to a turn: the job outlives its turn. The line is the job's
output, so a client shows it as text that a program wrote.

wakes_left.description: How many more matches may wake the model.

anyOf.description:
A contained job listens on a loopback port: efr forwarded it to the same port of
127.0.0.1, or says why not. It belongs to the conversation, not to a turn.

by_job.description: For `in_use`: the job of the same conversation that holds the port.

listen.description: The address that the job listens on, as text: `127.0.0.1`, `::1`.

outcome.description: What efr did with the port.

reason.description: For `refused` and `limit`: a short reason, such as `a service port`.

anyOf.description: A job ended. It belongs to the conversation, not to a turn.

blocked.description:
The connections that efr's proxy refused while the job ran, at most
[`SandboxSummary::MAX_BLOCKED`]. Absent when none.

blocked_more.description: The refusals that `blocked` leaves out. 0 when absent.

bus_refused.description:
The bus calls that the bus filter refused while the job ran (phase E), at
most [`SandboxSummary::MAX_BUS_REFUSED`]. Absent when none.

bus_refused_more.description: The refusals that `bus_refused` leaves out. 0 when absent.

exit_code.description: The exit status of its command, when it exited. Absent otherwise.

launcher_lost.description:
True when the job's launcher ended without its result, so the job's
processes may still run. False when absent.

output_bytes.description: The bytes that the job wrote to its output.

output_truncated.description:
True when efr could not write all of the output to the output file, such as
on a full disk; the tail is whole. False when absent.

quarantined.description:
True when at least one of those changes went to quarantine. False when
absent.

ran_secs.description: How long the job ran, in seconds.

stopped_by.description: Who or what stopped it. Absent for a job that ended by itself.

surface_changes.description:
The git settings and other files that run code, which the job changed.
Absent when none.

survivors.description:
The names of the job's processes that efr could not end, which may still
run. Absent when none.

tail.description:
The end of the output: at most 50 lines and 8 KiB. The job wrote it, so a
client shows it as text that a program wrote.

anyOf.description:
A job notice entered the conversation: a turn took it into its first message.
The notice is never the user's input. The turn records it before its
`turn_started`.

not_user_input.description: Always true: a notice is never the user's input.

notice_kind.description: What the notice tells. Not named `kind`, which names the event's kind.

source_seq.description:
The sequence number of the `job_ended` or `job_watch_matched` event that the
notice tells about.

text.description: The text of the notice, as the model read it.

turn_id.description: The turn that took the notice.

woke.description:
True when the notice started the turn; false when it rode in a turn that a
prompt started.

anyOf.description:
A job notice that could have started a turn did not, and waits for the next turn
that a prompt starts. Recorded once per notice. It belongs to the conversation,
not to a turn.

source_seq.description: The sequence number of the event that the notice tells about.

anyOf.description:
A command of a `shell` call still runs in the conversation's hidden shell after
its call answered the model, because the call's timeout passed. The shell takes
no other call until the command ends. The event belongs to the conversation, not
to a turn. It and the call's `tool_call_completed` (with `left_running`) can come
in either order: a client links them by `call_id`.

approved_by.description: Who approved the call. Absent when the call needed no approval.

call_id.description: The call whose command still runs.

command.description:
The first 200 characters of the command line. The model wrote it, so a client
shows it as text that a program wrote, on one line.

contained.description:
True when the command runs in the sandbox. A client never asks the user for a
hidden answer, an answer to a wait that looks secret, or a manual answer to a
command in the sandbox.

input.description: What the command waits for when its call answered.

looks_secret.description:
True for a `visible` wait whose prompt line looks like a password prompt, as
in [`Event::ToolCallInputChanged`]. False when absent.

prompt.description:
The row of the screen that holds the cursor while the command waits, at most
200 characters, such as `u@h's password:`. The program wrote it, so a client
shows it as text that a program wrote, on one line. Absent when the command
does not wait.

anyOf.description:
A command that a `shell` call left running in the hidden shell began or stopped
waiting for input. The daemon reports each change once. It belongs to the
conversation, not to a turn. A client that can read keys asks the user while the
latest `input` is not `none`, and sends the answer with `input.respond` and this
`call_id`.

call_id.description: The call whose command still runs.

contained.description: True when the command runs in the sandbox.

input.description: What the command waits for now.

looks_secret.description:
True for a `visible` wait whose prompt line looks like a password prompt.
False when absent.

prompt.description:
The row of the screen that holds the cursor, at most 200 characters. Absent
when the command does not wait.

anyOf.description:
A command that a `shell` call left running in the hidden shell ended, or left the
shell. The hidden shell is free again, unless `how` is `closed` or
`shell_exited`: then the next call starts a new shell. It belongs to the
conversation, not to a turn.

exit_code.description: The exit status of the command, when the shell reported it. Absent otherwise.

anyOf.description:
The user deleted the conversation (`conversation.delete`). It is the last event
of the conversation and the only one that stays in the log: efrd removes every
other event of the conversation after it, and the store refuses each later
event of it. A subscription of the conversation ends after it.

Event.description:
Something that happened, as the event log records it and subscribers receive it.

Variants are named `<Noun><PastParticiple>`. Each one carries the full state of what it
reports, never a delta against an earlier event, so a subscriber can resume from any
sequence number without reading anything else.

On the wire an event is one object whose `kind` member is the snake_case variant
name, such as `{"kind": "turn_started", ...}`. A kind that this build does not know
decodes as [`Event::Unknown`] and encodes back to the same JSON, so an old reader
keeps advancing its cursor past events from a newer daemon. A known kind with a
malformed body is an error, not `Unknown`.

A new variant needs a fixture in `fixtures/v1/events/`; a test fails until it has one.

EventEnvelope.description: An event with its place in the log.

at.description: When the daemon recorded the event.

conversation_id.description:
The conversation the event belongs to; absent for daemon-wide events such as
[`Event::LoginCompleted`] and [`Event::LogoutCompleted`].

ExitFacts.description: Facts about an exit that efr collected itself, never from the model or a tool.

denials_in_a_row.description: Classifier denials in a row without an allow or a person's answer.

desktop_read.description:
For a `desktop_ipc` exit: true when every desktop command of the line only reads
the desktop's state or reloads its config, such as `hyprctl monitors`.

git_code.description:
For an `outside` or `upload` exit of a git or gh line: the git code that the line
runs outside the sandbox, when it made the exit one that only the user may
approve: efr could not check it, or a sandboxed command can write a part of it.
Absent for any other exit, so a clean check is never a reason to allow. It holds
only the parts that a sandboxed command can write.

git_status.description: For a destructive exit: the counts of the hardened `git status`.

outside_commands.description:
For an `outside` exit: the commands of the line that run outside the sandbox,
such as `df -h`, in the order of the line.

previous_exits_this_turn.description:
The earlier exits of this turn and how each was judged: each a list of two, the
kind and then the verdict.

refusals_in_a_row.description: Floor refusals in a row without a person's answer.

repo_surface_changed_this_turn.description: True when a git setting or another file that runs code changed in this turn.

sandbox_export_names.description: The names, never the values, that sandboxed calls exported.

snapshot_covers.description:
True when efr's snapshot or its home store covers every target of the exit, so
`efr undo` can bring them back: the AND over the exit's needs. False is a higher
risk. Absent when no need has a target.

targets.description: The paths the action writes or reads.

upload_patterns.description: The upload patterns that the line matched, such as `git push`.

ExitInfo.description: What an approval question for an exit shows, on top of its one-line summary.

always.description:
The rule that an `allow_always` answer saves, in words, such as
`write under ~/notes` or `host download.example.org:443` (phase E). Absent when
no rule may cover the call; a client offers the answer only when it is set.

facts.description:
Facts that efr collected itself, one line each, such as `runs /usr/bin/python,
not .venv/bin/python` or `untrusted: written in the sandbox`.

grants.description: Exactly what a "yes" opens; empty for an unsandboxed launch.

judged.description: The classifier's answer, when it judged first and asked the user (phase 3).

kinds.description: The exits of the call, each kind once.

launch.description: How the call runs after a "yes".

model_reason.description: The model's reason from `needs`, shown labelled as the model's.

user_only.description: True when only the user may approve this exit.

ExitKind.description:
The kind of an exit: an action that the sandbox does not allow on its own.

Each kind has its own launch after a "yes" and its own approvers. A floor kind
([`ExitKind::is_floor`]) is denied before any question.

oneOf.description: A write outside the write roots.
A network host (phase 1: any network use).
A view of the host's network (`ss`, `ip addr`).
A Unix socket of a tool.
A desktop's IPC socket (`swaymsg`, `xrandr`): it can type or run commands.
A message bus.
A device node.
A read of a sandbox mask, such as a project `.env`.
A destructive action inside the write roots, such as `git reset --hard`.
The model asked to run outside the sandbox.
`sudo` and other ways to more rights.
A change that runs later: rc files, services, cron, a floor path.

InputRespond.description:
The params of `input.respond`: one line that the user typed for a running tool call
whose last `tool_call_input_changed` event said that it waits for input.

The daemon writes `text` and then a carriage return to the call's PTY, but only
while that call's command runs, the wait it reported last is of the answer's kind
(hidden with `hidden`, visible without) and the job that waited still holds the
terminal, and with `hidden` only while the PTY also reads a line with echo off. A
`manual` answer needs no reported wait: it is written while that call's command runs
and the job that the daemon's last look saw, not the shell itself, holds the
terminal, and never for a call whose command types into a shell that reads command
lines (a `nested_shell` call, or a command that starts a shell or a REPL), where it
would run as a command line. The daemon answers
`not_found` for an unknown conversation or when no call's command runs in it (the
call ended, so an answer after its `tool_call_completed` always gets `not_found`, or
its command was left at its timeout and goes on without a call), `conflict` when
another call's command runs or the call's command does not wait for that input, and
`invalid` for a text that is not one line. Then it writes nothing.

There is no command id: like `pty.write`, an answer is never retried, so the daemon
keeps no receipt, which would also store the text. `Debug` never shows the text.

call_id.description: The call that waits for input.

conversation_id.description: The conversation of the running call.

hidden.description:
True when the client asked the user for hidden input, because the event said
`hidden`; false for `visible`. The daemon refuses an answer of the other kind. With
`hidden` it also requires the PTY's echo to be off when it writes, so the terminal
does not put the text in the output that the model reads.

manual.description:
True when the user chose to type an input for a command that reported no wait,
such as one that printed nothing for a while (`Ctrl+\` in `efr`). The daemon
then skips the check against a reported wait and its kind, and keeps the others.
False when absent.

text.description:
The line without its line ending: at most [`InputRespond::MAX_TEXT_BYTES`] bytes
and no control characters (U+0000 to U+001F and U+007F). The daemon never logs or
records it.

InputRespondResult.description: The result of `input.respond`: the line was written to the call's PTY.

InputWait.description:
Whether a running tool call's command waits for the user to type a line, and what
happens to that line.

oneOf.description: The call does not wait for input now, so a client stops asking the user.

The command waits for an answer that is not read like a password, such as a
`[Y/n]` question. On a plain terminal the answer is echoed and reaches the output
that the model reads. Through a relay such as `sudo`'s own pty, the program on
the inner terminal decides whether the answer is shown, and the model then reads
what is shown; a password prompt of a program behind such a relay is reported
as visible too.

The command reads a line with echo off, such as the password prompt of `sudo` or
`ssh`. The user's answer is not shown and the terminal does not put it in the
output; the model sees it only if the program that reads it prints it.

Mode.description:
The permission mode of a turn: the base policy, which the user's own rules follow and
win over where they match.

Some floors hold in every mode: a privileged program such as `sudo` asks, secrets
are denied unless a user rule names them, and no tool writes efr's config. Full mode
keeps these floors and the other questions that `docs/permissions.md` names in its
section "Full mode"; the other modes also ask for an interactive call. A turn from a
remote origin runs with at most [`Mode::Cautious`].

The variants are ordered from the strictest to the loosest, so the remote cap is
`mode.min(Mode::Cautious)`.

oneOf.description: Every call asks, except what the user's own rules allow.

The built-in rules that let commands and files be read without a question. The
default.

Shell commands run at once in a kernel sandbox (bubblewrap, Landlock and
seccomp): they can write only in the turn's project, the registered projects
that the command names, `$SCRATCH`, a private `/tmp` and private tool caches, and
they have no network. An action that leaves the sandbox is an exit, and the user
answers it. When the sandbox is not available, a turn runs as `cautious` and
[`EffectiveSettings::fallback`] says why.

Every call runs at once as the user, with no sandbox and no question. efr still
reads each line for a small set of floors (`docs/permissions.md`, "Full mode").
The user allows it with `permissions.allow_full`; a phone turn runs with at most
`cautious`, a turn that a job notice starts with at most `auto`.

Why a turn that asked for one mode runs with a stricter one: `auto` without a
working sandbox, or in a project at the home directory, runs as `cautious`, and a

reason.description:

A loopback port of a contained job that efr forwards to the same port of

PresenceSet.description:
The params of `presence.set`. Any later input of an attached client sets the

conversation_id.description:

The conversations whose presence changed, each with one `presence_changed`

oneOf.description: Input of an attached client.
The user, with `presence.set` (`efr away`, `,away`).
No input for `presence.away_after_minutes`.

ProgramFact.description: A program word of the line.

changed_this_turn.description: True when the program changed in this turn.

in_write_root.description: True when the program lies in a write root.

resolved.description:
Where it resolves: the absolute path of a file, or `builtin`, a relative path,
